newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Lott sees Pena confirmation vote in week.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Lott sees Pena confirmation vote in week.

text.p: The full U.S. Senate likely will vote within a week on whether to confirm Federico Pena as the next energy secretary, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Thursday.
The Senate Energy Committee earlier Thursday voted 19-0 to send Pena's nomination on to the full Senate after several weeks of delay.
"I would like to get that up today. There is some indication there may be an objection and we may not be able to get that up until next week either," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, told reporters.
"But my expectation is within a week we will have a vote on the Pena nomination," Lott said.

Minnesota Republican Sen. Rod Grams earlier Thursday said he wanted to put off Pena's Senate confirmation vote until the White House clarifies its position on how to dispose of radioactive waste from utilities' nuclear power reactors.
The federal government by law assumes responsiblity for that waste next year.
